steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: It's hard to believe that you're leaving, Lady Heidi, after all the effort it took to return to this great city.

steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: But perhaps it's time you returned to your father.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Back to Toron? Well... maybe I'll go further than that. My father is not the only guide I have in life.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Your advice has been most enlightening, of course, such as your story of dinner with the envoy of the Earl of March.

steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: It's my pleasure to offer first-hand information to an aspiring novelist who is not involved in the political world.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Or perhaps, I will write my familiar homeland of Toron into the story of this terrible war in Londinium.

steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: Yes, it can be painful to recall those shameful times, but someone must remember the heroic deeds we performed for the city.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Heroic... you're right. Maybe we're all heroes.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: How about a love story: a girl from the Victorian borderlands falls in love with a young man who came on holiday, but the young man dies on the battlefields of Londinium.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: In the end, though, the news of the young man's death turns out to be false, and he returns to her side a hero.

steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: A brilliant idea, Lady Heidi. A love lost and found again, just like a city trampled by outsiders, but saved by our hands.

steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: Hear, the orchestra plays. There is no wine or dessert, and the candles do not burn as bright, but the music remains beautiful.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: By all means, join the dance. Leave me on this balcony with the inspiration you've supplied.

steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: What about your friends here—

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: An emissary from a foreign land, yet unfamiliar with Victorian customs. Surely you will forgive him?

steps.name: Pompous Man
steps.text: Of course, of course.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Lady Heidi, is that right?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: —Ah, I can show you around the place.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: N—No, we shouldn't bother you any more than we already have. Thank you for the assist.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: This place turns away no one. Next time, you should come in through the front door rather than the balcony, though.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Thank you for the offer, but... I'm not that interested in noble parties, to be honest.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Victorian noble politics was the first thing I studied before I came. I'm familiar with your customs, your attitudes toward the Infected, even your dance steps...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Setting aside whether a third-rate novelist would call herself noble... have you asked this soldier why she brought you here?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Sh—She didn't make me come here. I insisted on coming.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: I apologize, Lady Heidi. He said he wanted to stay in Londinium and learn more about our Infected problem, so I was taking him around... in less-than-conventional ways, sometimes.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: You can laugh if you want. You see how he is; not at all adept at lying or concealing his thoughts.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Rather fits the Pure Heart name, doesn't it?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Eliseo, representative of Pure Heart Medical?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I didn't expect our reputation to precede us...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: It's easy to recognize the people who are interested in the Infected problem.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Less easy to see through the concerted deception of the nobility.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: —Like how most of the people stepping onto the dance floor are Infected.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: That's to be expected, in theory at least. The Originium particles that the Sarkaz spread don't discriminate according to social status. But...

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Nobody will say it out loud. Nobody asks if they're standing next to an Infected. It's about appearances... and a dream.

Eliseo gazes at the hall. There are holes on pillars where golden ornaments once glittered, a testament to the looting during the war, but the passionate playing of the musicians is almost enough to cover up the desolation.
The self-proclaimed novelist opens the cap of her fountain pen and scribbles in a notebook.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: You could call it meaningless self-consolation, at a time when basic livelihood is in question.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: No, not at all.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Just different ways of living.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: What is that?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The shadow of a synopsis... and a little extra information. I would like you to take it.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I have a feeling we will meet again, Eliseo.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: If you don't mind me asking, though—you seem to be holding onto some pain that this banquet can't soothe.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I'm just missing a friend of mine.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: There's one less person who will speak with me frankly, now that she's gone.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The Summit of Nations?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The Lateran is paying close attention to the events in Victoria. After all, this is a disaster caused by the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: However, the decisiveness that you and Parliament have shown on the Sarkaz question gave me hope for the city's revival.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Of course, His Holiness sincerely wishes to build the bridge of peace for the nations of Terra, in order to prevent another tragedy from happening.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You're not only here on behalf of His Holiness the Lateran Pope, are you?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I am but a humble Messenger, here to deliver a message to you and Parliament.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Then please send my apologies to His Holiness. I appreciate the kindness that Laterano is demonstrating, but Parliament is not in a position to address matters beyond Londinium.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Kindly inform the duke currently playing host to you that I am not going to Laterano in any capacity. As for his own plans, those have never been any business of Parliament nor myself, have they?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Of course. That's what Messengers are for.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Oren Argiolas. He was on Duke Gododdin's battleship during the war, but never participated directly on behalf of Laterano.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Just as I thought. Does Gododdin have a sweet tooth too?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: If so, we don't have much for him here in Londinium.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: So much for Parliament's day off.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: One interesting tidbit. The Lateran Messenger went onto the ship with a group of refugees. He made an oath by placing his hand on his gun, in order to convince the Duke to accept the refugees.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The scorching hot barrel gave him a blister on his hand.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Hah, that's out of nowhere. Is it important?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Day off.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Alright, I've been off. Now, which message should I read first? Investigation report on the Arts Circle remnants?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Oh?
Vina sees Lieutenant Shearer's name. Another letter.
She sighs and drops it in the 'Pending' bin.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Delphine, is this—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Hey, Vina! We caught those robbers you were on about and taught 'em a lesson!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Targeting frail Oripathy patients. Scum.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You know what's even worse? We got a bunch of cowardly wankers who wanted to join the ranks.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: It's a good job you got the news quick and didn't give them a chance to grow.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I wish I could go out and move about.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Don't worry, I gave 'em an extra punch for you.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: And I saved your share of the thank-you gift.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Wait, we're not collecting protection money—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: When was the last time you had candy since we got back to Victoria?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Indra...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: The lad who got robbed said he made 'em himself. A risk with every mouthful! It's not like you ever liked normal candy sticks.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: He said he couldn't get his hands on regular sweeteners, so he's tried potatoes, carrots, Originium slug fluids...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I tried all of 'em. Didn't throw up or nuffin.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Sounds like a real pick-me-up. Can I try one?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Sure! There's plenty.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Are you okay, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Fine. I've had worse.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: What about your Speaker duties?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Yeah, what are you worried about right now? New laws? Announcements? Reports?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Any work you need us to do? Especially the ones that involve punching which you can't do yourself.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I even took on a new lackey today! He's built like a straw, but I can teach him a few moves to defend himself.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: It's time for Glasgow to rebuild. When can we go back—
Indra scratches her head. She did not need her friends' reproaching glances to realize she should not have asked.
Vina glances across her desk, where the mountain of papers has not grown any thinner.
Delphine walks to her side and takes the letters that she was holding.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I think it's time to give a public answer to the issues that concern our citizens. Most don't come to listen to Parliamentary debate, but they'll listen to the radio at the end of a long day.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The situation in the city is stabilizing. I've requested a third engineering team for Norport. Soon, our home will be back to the way it was.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: BETTER than the way it was.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You can go back to Lynncardine, Delphine, once we've taken care of this business.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Diane?

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Lieutenant?!

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I'm retired... Sarah.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Oh, okay. Sir.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: I thought you had declined the Sanatorium's invitation.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Just coming to visit, and to thank you again... I hope you don't mind.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: I don't remember much, to be honest. The doctors say the rocks have gone into my head—your hands are trembling.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: No need to hide it from me, sir. I haven't forgotten what you taught me.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Looks like addiction symptoms. From the war?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Excessive painkiller use. After that thing at the walls.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: You must stay. I'll go for a doctor. Maybe they can...

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: At least find you some—

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: More painkillers? Yeah, maybe that would soothe the pain.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: That's why you're here, isn't it? Supplies are short, but maybe they can spare some.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Lady Delphine has been very good to the Sanatorium, and to us.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Just a moment. I'll be right back.
He wants to stay. Maybe he could really get some painkillers, even if there is little enough to spare.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Phew—

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Oh, where did he go?

steps.name: Passerby
steps.text: Hey, watch where you're going!

steps.name: Passerby
steps.text: Whoa, keep your distance. Something's not right with him.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: The Speaker's office is... this way... argh...

steps.name: Passerby
steps.text: He just toppled over! Another of those poor Infected sods?

steps.name: Passerby
steps.text: Stay away from him! We're all goners if he shatters...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I'm... not... argh... my body... I can't...

steps.name: Passerby
steps.text: I'll go get someone! Keep your distance, everyone!
Shearer collapses on the street. The rays of the setting sun are not particularly bright, but they are enough to hurt his eyes.
Or, perhaps, it is his body's way of reminding him that only another deep-seated desire can mask the pain.
He tries to adjust his breathing, like he instructed the soldiers fighting pain during the war...
But he fails. He has already lost the fight.
Shearer sees fire. It is so hot he cannot open his eyes. The sky burns. The walls burn. He burns—
He sees the day when he lay on the ground beneath the walls.
The walls of Londinium burned with Draco fire, burning brighter and brighter, until the flames consumed the sky.
He cries out in fear, and tries to cover his eyes—
...Lieutenant...
Lieutenant... Shearer... wake... up...
He sees a hand reach out towards him.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: ...Lady Delphine?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I have been waiting for you, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I saw the letter you wrote to Vina... but you avoided me, just like you refused my offer of treatment.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: She never read my letter... did she, Lady Delphine?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I can guess what you wrote.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'm sorry, but I can't help you here. We both know the state of medicine availability in Londinium. You can't stay here.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Where can I go?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Lynncardine.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: No! I...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I wasn't asking, Lieutenant. This is an order. And don't give me that excuse about being retired.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I know why you hesitate. I know what you fear.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You're afraid to face the senior officers who betrayed and abandoned you at Irnclad Galavae...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You're afraid that you won't come good on your loyalty to me and my mother, and you're afraid to return home like this. Aren't you?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I... I don't know...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You're not as strong as you think, Lieutenant. And I'm not as weak, or noble, as you think.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Our home is Lynncardine. Not here.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The war is over, Lieutenant. This soldier should go home.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't be afraid. I'm going home with you.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: (Sob) But how... how do I make it home, when I'm like this...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'll take care of it. Did you really think I would abandon you just because you didn't come looking for me?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Thank you... Lady Delphine...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Will you return to Londinium?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Yes. I promised Vina. But she may have to wait.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'll make arrangements for you to get treatment. We'll depart once I've taken care of what I have in front of me.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Yes, my Lady.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Lynncardine... I'm coming home, Mother.
